messages:
ashley: Heads up — saw steady RSS growth on canary with prefix-prefetch=on and session_stickiness=enabled. Repro: longctx load (~24k tokens/user) over 45m shows +820MB RSS vs baseline.

michael: which commit & kernel-select change?

ashley: rolled canary back to main@2026-03-10 (before the kernel-select tweak) — still reproduces. Quick log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] kv_cache: alloc_page id=0x7fffa1 size=4096 owner=session:abc
[2026-03-10T14:17:40Z] kv_cache: page_evicted id=0x7fffa1 reason=frag
RSS +812MB over 45m
```

sam: that smells like fragmentation from key aliasing. Are we canonicalizing prefixes differently per request?

ashley: maybe. I tested with tenant_salt=off (deterministic hash) — reuse hitrate dropped ~18% which hurts latency/cost. With salt on we get better reuse but more tiny pages that don't coalesce.

priya: another angle: batching holds KV refs longer. If batch_size>1 we keep pages pinned across the micro-batches, which delays eviction and increases fragmentation. Kernel selection that picks wide attention kernels for longctx can extend KV lifetime too.

perf-bot: perf/run/longctx-2026-03-11 completed: prefetch=on sticky=on | p50 latency +3ms | tokens/sec -4% | memory delta +780MB

michael: can you dump a heap/pprof (meta vs value bytes)? Need to know if fragments are metadata overhead or actual KV value bytes.

ashley: pprof excerpt pasted: 
```
heap_alloc: 820MB
kv_pages: 612MB (nodes: 15k)
other: 208MB
```

sam: 15k nodes => lots of small fragments. Two immediate ideas: (1) change canonicalization to a global prefix fingerprint (sha1) so aliases collide into same key, (2) run a background compaction that merges adjacent small pages when tenant matches. Also consider coarse TTL bump on session_stickiness routes to avoid indefinite pinning.

priya: +1. Also propose an evict_on_batch_complete flag: decrement refs when batch finishes instead of waiting for full request lifecycle. Quick workaround: disable session_stickiness on known longctx routes.

ashley: I'll run two experiments today: evict_on_batch_complete=true on canary, and a low-cost compaction pass that coalesces pages <4KB if neighbors free and same tenant. Will measure reuse hitrate, p50, and memory delta.

michael: if you can, include a run with kernel-select pinned to older heuristic to rule out kernel lifetime interaction. If compaction helps we can land a safe canary.

infra-bot: canary deployed to fleet-group=kv-leak-debug at 3305554350

ashley: thanks infra-bot — starting runs now. Will post numbers when finished.

michael: thanks. if we see reuse drop too much, we might try hybrid canonicalization: fingerprint + tenant scoped alias map.

ashley: noted. Will try fingerprint + map only if compaction evicts too much reuse.

sam: also add a small profiler hook to sample page owner lifetimes, it's cheap and will help root cause.

ashley: adding hook. back with numbers in ~2h. :white_check_mark:
